local_articles.title: Seeds Rybakina, Pegula, Gauff reach third round at WTA Toronto
local_articles.snippet: TORONTO – Second seed Elena Rybakina, third seed Jessica Pegula and fourth-seeded Coco Gauff all advanced to the third round of the WTA 1000 tournament in Toronto on Aug 5 . local_articles.title: Dutch shocks for Zverev, Medvedev as seeds fall in Canadian Open
local_articles.snippet: Aug 6 - Alexander Zverev and Daniil Medvedev both suffered upsets against Dutch opponents in the second round of the Canadian Open on Wednesday, while fellow title contender Taylor Fritz also crashed out in Montreal. World number three Zverev, playing his first match since losing to Jannik Sinner in last month's Wimbledon final, was beaten 6-7(3) 6-2 6-4 by Tallon Griekspoor, who arrived in Canada with one win in his last eight tour-level matches. The defeat comes as a setback to the German's preparations for the U.S. Open, which begins on August 30. "I've been very close to throwing in the towel a couple of times," world number 69 Griekspoor said after claiming his third victory over French Open champion Zverev. questions.title: Which country will the Spanish Football Federation announce as the host of the 2027 Spanish Super Cup?
questions.background: The Spanish Super Cup features the winners and runners-up of La Liga and the Copa del Rey. Saudi Arabia has hosted the competition since 2020.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Spanish Football Federation’s official host announcement, corroborated by reliable news reporting. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the country officially named as host of the 2027 Spanish Super Cup by August 31, 2026. This question concerns the announced host, not whether the tournament subsequently takes place there. Resolution occurs when the announcement is made. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the host country, rather than the host city or stadium.
questions.current_reasoning: Saudi Arabia cannot host the 2027 Spanish Super Cup in January due to hosting the AFC Asian Cup (Jan 7–Feb 6, 2027), and RFEF president Rafael Louzán repeatedly pointed to Doha, Qatar as the leading one-off replacement while extending Saudi Arabia's broader contract to 2030. However, April 2026 Spanish press reports (AS, Mundo Deportivo) noted no official confirmation yet, flagged Middle East geopolitical uncertainty (US–Iran conflict affecting Qatar/Finalissima), and confirmed RFEF plans to shift the tournament to February 2027. Qatar remains the clear favorite (58%), with realistic fallback probabilities on Spain (16%), Saudi Arabia hosting after the Asian Cup ends on Feb 6 (10%), UAE (7%), Morocco (5%), and a 4% tail elsewhere.
